answer: In an agent market for sonnet recordings and ivory-colored artwork, charge voting influence to coins irreversibly burned. A ticket names its election, beneficiary and burn transaction; validators verify the destruction, mark the receipt spent and weight votes by the amount burned. A ripple of new accounts cannot turn one burned coin into many votes. More influence requires more destroyed value, so an attacker must acquire and sacrifice extra coins. Wealthy attackers can still buy power; the rule prices influence without proving unique people.
